title: Crewship panel payload — metric.v1
description: One number, with an optional delta, target and sparkline. Pushed by a routine or by a script running inside a crew container: `crewship page set <page>/<panel> --data -` reading this document on stdin. The panel holds no query and no datasource — this payload IS the panel's data, and the server attaches the timestamp, the run id and the producer identity to it. Freshness (fresh / stale / failed) is computed server-side from the timestamp the server stored, so there is deliberately no field here in which a producer could supply its own.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference (informational; the server ignores it). Present so a hand-written payload gets inline validation in an editor while a producer script is being developed.

value.description: The measured value, rendered at full contrast when fresh. Required, and nullable on purpose: `0` is a measured zero ("we looked and there was nothing") and `null` is no basis to compute ("we have nothing to look at"), which renders as an em dash. The two are different claims and the app already separates them — do not send 0 to mean "no data".

unit.description: Unit suffix rendered next to the value ("ms", "req/s", "Kč"). One unit per panel: two units is two panels, because a single tile cannot say which number the unit belongs to.

delta.description: Change since the previous push, in the same unit as `value`. Omit when there is no previous value to compare against; send 0 when the value genuinely did not move — an omitted delta renders as nothing, a zero delta renders as "no change".

delta_good.description: Which direction of `delta` is an improvement, and the only thing that lets the delta take a colour. Omit it and the delta renders with its sign, an arrow and a muted tone; send "up" and a rise is success, send "down" and a fall is success. There is no default on purpose: green-up on an error rate would be a lie, so the payload has to say which way is good.

target.description: The value this metric is aiming at, in the same unit. Rendered as a marker, never as a second series.

items.description: One historical point. `null` marks a gap the producer knows about, so the line breaks instead of interpolating across missing data.

sparkline.description: Recent history for the inline trend line, oldest first. Bounded at 200 to match the payload ring: a panel is not a time-series database, and a longer array is payload bloat rather than more insight. Around 30 points is what the rendered sparkline can actually resolve.
